body:
Good morning, Bakersfield — it’s Sunday, August 30, 2026. Today’s top story is the return of NFL star Aaron Donald to the Los Angeles Rams after a two-and-a-half-year retirement. We’re waking up to a warm morning, with temperatures already at 86° at Meadows Field and an expected high of 92° later today. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 74, and no weather alerts are active in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Kern County saw a series of incidents that kept law enforcement busy. The most significant call came around 11:26 p.m., when crews responded to a tractor-trailer fire on Pacheco Road. By 11:35, the tractor was reported as a total loss, though the trailer was salvaged. Around the same time, shortly before midnight, a caller reported hearing a shot fired from inside his living room; medical units were on scene. Later, around 2:48 a.m., officers went to Ginger Oak Lane for a welfare check after a crying caller reported a baby in the background. A subject was later seen running through the carport toward a warehouse, and units held the perimeter. Elsewhere, around 12:58 a.m., a large party on Potomac Avenue near Oswell Street turned into a physical fight, with one caller reporting possible shots — though it was unclear whether fireworks were involved. In addition, around 10:08 p.m., a man threatened to shoot the reporting party’s husband during a verbal dispute at a Bakersfield apartment complex. No weapon was seen at first, but the same subject was later seen walking through the complex with a baseball bat. Other incidents included a collision near Panama Lane and Ashe Road that required a tow, a verbal dispute with a possible gunshot heard, and a physical fight at an apartment on H Street.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 92° and a low around 62° tonight. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 74. Skies are expected to be clear, making for a warm late-summer day across the county.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Aaron Donald has ended his two-and-a-half-year retirement and will return to the Los Angeles Rams.** The NFL star’s decision to come back to the field after an extended break is expected to bring a significant boost to the Rams’ defensive line. This move has generated excitement among fans and analysts alike, as Donald’s return promises to add depth and experience to the team’s roster for the upcoming season.

**According to 23ABC, the League of Dreams tipped off its 2026 basketball season with more than 140 athletes and a new mascot.** The event, held at Riverlakes Ranch Community Center, marked a milestone for the organization that provides adaptive sports opportunities for athletes with disabilities. The gym filled with cheers as teams came together for the season opener, and the Cal State Bakersfield women’s basketball team made a special appearance. Board Vice President Laura Avila emphasized that community support makes the programs possible, and the season also introduced the league’s first-ever mascot, Dreamer.

**KGET 17 also reports that a man accused of posing as an NFL player to scam women allegedly tricked AI and Google, according to court documents.** The suspect, who has not been named, is said to have used sophisticated methods to deceive his victims, highlighting the evolving nature of online scams. The case underscores the importance of vigilance in the digital age, as technology can sometimes be exploited for fraudulent purposes.

**23ABC said the USS Abraham Lincoln sailed past Singapore on its way home from the Middle East.** The U.S. aircraft carrier, one of the Navy’s largest warships, was supporting the U.S. war against Iran during its deployment. Its transit near Singapore early Sunday morning comes after a grueling deployment that included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 250 days. The Lincoln is expected to stop in Thailand for a port visit before returning to its base in San Diego, following concerns about the crew’s mental health and supply shortages during the lengthy deployment.

**KGET 17 also announced that thousands of cold remedy nasal swabs have been recalled nationwide.** The recall affects a specific batch of the product and is due to potential contamination concerns. Consumers are advised to check the batch numbers of their nasal swabs and to discontinue use if they have the affected product. Further details on the recall and instructions for returning the product are expected to be released by the manufacturer.

**23ABC reported that Nova Sorella hosted a resource fair in Bakersfield to honor the founder’s son.** The nonprofit brought together organizations such as Serving Hope and The Open Door Network to connect community members with essential services. PJ Jones, founder and executive director of Nova Sorella, organized the fair in honor of her son, Ty Jr. Jones, who was killed by gun violence in January 2017. The event, held on what would have been Ty Jr.’s birthday, aimed to bring hope to an underserved community and provided attendees with resources for work, housing, and more.

## Something good

The League of Dreams tipped off its 2026 basketball season with more than 140 athletes and a new mascot. This event highlights the community’s commitment to providing inclusive sports opportunities for local youth, and the debut of the organization’s first-ever mascot, Dreamer, added to the excitement. Board Vice President Laura Avila noted that community support makes the programs possible, and the season opener was a heartwarming display of the impact adaptive sports can have on athletes and their families.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several events and meetings are on the calendar for Kern County residents. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater will host a variety of shows, including the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 starting on August 24, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4, The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies also on September 4, Talib Kweli -- One Night Only In Bakersfield on September 5, JUSTIN WILLMAN: ONE FOR THE AGES TOUR on September 10, and MAX AMINI LIVE IN BAKERSFIELD! on September 12.

For those interested in local government, the Police Civil Service Commission will meet on September 2 at 8:30 a.m., the Planning Commission will convene on September 3 at 5:30 p.m., and the Personnel and Processes Committee will gather on September 2 at 12:00 p.m. These meetings provide opportunities for community members to engage with local officials and stay informed about important issues affecting Kern County.
